chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Jameela al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who bequeathed a sword to a man. So the inheritors said, 'You have only the iron, and the ornaments are not for you; other than the iron is not for you.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote to me: 'The sword is for him, and its ornaments.'
ai.seo_question: Does bequeathing a sword include its hilt and scabbard in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the principle of *al-asl yajibu ma yajibu lahu al-tabi'* (the principal entails its accessories) in Islamic inheritance law. It clarifies that unless specified otherwise, a bequeathed sword includes its hilt and scabbard, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the natural association of components unless explicitly severed by the testator's intent.
